questions.question: Why should Consultative Prompting be taught as a workflow instead of only as tool awareness?
options: Because teams need shared signals, controls, and decision rules they can apply to real work
Because AI removes the need for review
questions.explanation: The lesson is designed around reusable operating artifacts so teams can apply the topic in project decisions, not just recognize tool names.

questions.question: Which signal is explicitly part of this lesson?
questions.explanation: The lesson uses "unclear decision" as one of the concrete signals for deciding what action or control is needed.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce for Consultative Prompting?
options: A ranked plan with category, score, priority, controls, and rationale
questions.explanation: The artifact is a classroom planner that turns scenarios into structured recommendations and reusable controls.

questions.question: Which control belongs to the lesson design?
options: Treating all AI outputs as facts
questions.explanation: The control "assumption check" is part of the intended operating model for this topic.

questions.question: When should a scenario become a launch-gate discussion rather than a casual awareness exercise?
options: When impact, uncertainty, and matched risk signals are high
Only when the model is open source
Only when the user interface is complex
Never; all AI topics should be handled informally
questions.explanation: High-impact, uncertain, or risk-heavy scenarios require stronger controls and explicit launch decisions.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the output template?
options: To create a reusable worksheet or prompt that teams can apply after the course
questions.explanation: Each lesson ships an artifact that helps participants apply the capability in their daily workflow.
